verdict.rationale: Nix's own docs say `nix-shell` builds or downloads a project's declared dependencies and opens a shell with all needed environment variables set. They also document `nix develop` for the build environment, describe automatic setup of a package's build environment, and note binary caches that skip building from source. A community user confirms Nix works well for multi-language dev projects where virtualenv-style tools fail. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of the repo-file convention (shell.nix/flake.nix in a clone) that drives the one-command flow; Nix itself must be installed first via a separate installer, so a truly fresh machine needs two steps; no hands-on report of a clone-to-ready-shell walkthrough.
